mechanism: The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism prices the embedded emissions of imported iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity. source_location: Reg. 2023/956 Art. 3(34) (indirect emissions: electricity consumed in production, 'irrespective of the location of the production of the consumed electricity'), Art. 7(1) and Annex II (only direct emissions for iron and steel, aluminium and hydrogen; cement and fertilisers are not in Annex II), Art. 30(2)(a) (possible extension to embedded indirect emissions of Annex II goods), Art. 32 (transitional period 1 Oct 2023 to 31 Dec 2025), Art. 36(2) (Arts 21-27 and 31 apply from 1 Jan 2026); procedure 2025/0419(COD) summary (about 180 steel- and aluminium-intensive downstream products 'from 2028'; revised rules for attributing emissions to electricity); FTA release PDF p. 3 ('forward-looking most-favoured nation assurance', 'recognition of carbon prices, recognition of verifiers', 'financial assistance and targeted support'); Ministry of Steel taxonomy page (release and gazette dates)
notes: Context. CBAM applies only to India's exports to the EU, and no official Indian figure gives the tonnage that will switch route or its electricity, so nothing is sized. Direction: more EAF and hydrogen-DRI raises electricity per tonne; hydrogen for steel is inside green_hydrogen. Grid or captive: integrated steel plants and aluminium smelters run largely on captive power, outside NPP by the organisers' ruling; if Art. 30 extends CBAM to the indirect emissions of steel and aluminium, smelters would be pushed from captive coal to clean power, which raises NPP generation only if they buy it from the grid. India's Green Steel Taxonomy is reported to count Scope 1, Scope 2 and limited Scope 3 emissions against a 2.2 tCO2e per tonne threshold (PIB release 2083839 of 12 Dec 2024; PIB refused automated access here, so confirm in the gazette notification of 23 Dec 2024); if so, domestic certification also rewards low-carbon electricity. The FTA release lists an MFN assurance and cooperation, not an exemption. Links: industrial_electrification_green_steel (scale: steel electricity 94 TWh in 2021-22 and 184 TWh in 2030-31, mostly captive) and carbon_market_ccts (recognition of carbon prices).
